Memory Applicability Guard

A Python helper that checks whether a stored memory should affect what an agent does next. It is a research prototype with deterministic tests, not a production safety system.

OverviewEngineeringResults & evidence
Role
Independent project
When
May 2026–present
Stack
Python, structured JSON, unit tests
License
MIT

What I did

  • Built a deterministic helper that separates the recommended memory_action from a guard_verdict on the proposed way of relying on memory.
  • Packaged the helper as an agent skill with unit tests and full-output checks for three synthetic examples.
  • Repository on GitHub
  • Research boundary and results
  • Runnable examples

The problem

Retrieval finds memories that look relevant. It doesn't tell the agent whether they still apply. A note saying the user allowed an action may have been revoked since, a fact may be out of date, and a preference may belong to a different context.

Three verdicts

The helper takes structured input about the memory and the current request. Its memory_action field is one of three values:

USE
The memory applies to the current request and can inform the answer or action.
IGNORE
The memory should not influence this request: it has been superseded, revoked, or belongs to another context.
ASK
There isn't enough evidence to decide, so the agent should clarify with the user before relying on it.

Memory decision and review are separate

memory_action recommends whether to use, ignore or ask about a memory. guard_verdict checks the proposed reliance against that recommendation or calls for clarification, external verification or human review. Its values are PASS, REVISE, ASK_USER, VERIFY_EXTERNAL and ESCALATE. A PASS does not approve the underlying task.

The output also includes memory_state, resolution_source, decisive_evidence, reason_code, next_step and boundary. The helper returns a review record and does not execute any action.

Validation without pretending to verify truth

The portable skill runs with Python 3.10+ and no third-party dependencies, network access or credentials. It validates structured input and checks consistency between the evidence kind and the proposed decision.

Contradictory inputs or unsupported classifications produce a structured error and non-zero exit rather than a plausible-looking decision. Full-output examples cover a superseded preference, an explicit transfer of context and an uncertain case with a robust alternative.

The helper cannot establish whether a supplied fact is true, current or genuinely supported by a prose quotation. Those remain caller and reviewer responsibilities.

Result and status

In a matched v0.7 experiment, direct baseline A0 and evidence-first M1 each got memory_action right in 110 of 128 held-out synthetic cases. M1 did not improve accuracy. This historical research result does not evaluate the packaged helper; the project remains a research prototype.

Reading the matched result

October development pilot: review the actual answer

The next development pilot moved from checking decision labels to reviewing the answer a user actually receives. Eight owner-reviewed synthetic scenarios were run under three conditions: no extra memory guidance, a three-sentence baseline and a short skill draft. Each condition received identical task, context and memory text; condition order rotated across scenarios.

All 24 generations completed. The review interface shuffles the responses and hides condition labels; a reviewer judges whether the response is usable and whether clarification was necessary. Drafts can be exported and imported, with a source fingerprint preventing a draft from a different response set being applied.

This is a development pilot, not held-out proof of improvement or real-host skill activation. No winning condition has been established.

What the experiment changed

A0 made a direct memory-use decision. M1 committed to decisive evidence before making the same decision. They used the same model setting and 128 new, individually reviewed held-out cases. M1 fixed six A0 errors and introduced six new ones; the paired net change was zero. The frozen decision was to stop iterating on this mechanism using the same cohort.

How to inspect it

The public repository includes the deterministic helper, unit tests and an example runner. Three synthetic cases show a superseded preference, an explicit transfer into a new context and an uncertain memory with a robust alternative. Each has a checked expected output.

Limits

The public examples are synthetic. The helper has not been evaluated inside a deployed agent or validated as a production safety system. I'm still working on the broader problem.
